extracted.intended_audience: Investigators and research teams preparing NIH grant applications (especially R01 and K08 applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Using NIAID-posted sample R01 and K08 applications as exemplars to learn strong grantsmanship: how to present project goals, evidence, plans, and respond to review criteria while following current NIH forms and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of project goals, plans, and milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: How did the applicants present project goals, plans, and milestones in an appealing and clear way?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reviewing sample applications, note clarity, logical sequencing, how milestones are defined and tied to aims, and whether presentation is compelling/appealing to reviewers. Use these examples to inform organization and narrative choices in your own application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence and support provided; technical level of explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: What evidence and support did the applicants provide? How technical were the explanations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the appropriateness and sufficiency of preliminary data, citations, methodology detail, and rationale. Consider whether explanations balance necessary technical detail for expert review while remaining comprehensible to a broader review panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing each review criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how did the application effectively address each review criterion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map application sections to NIH review criteria (e.g., significance, investigators, innovation, approach, environment) and examine explicit statements or content that respond to those criteria. Use samples to identify wording, section placement, and evidence used to satisfy reviewers' expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-identified strengths and weaknesses (summary statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: What strong points (or potential weak points) did the reviewers highlight in the summary statements?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read accompanying summary statements to see what reviewers praised or critiqued. Use those comments to understand how reviewers interpreted the application, and to identify common pitfalls or effective strategies to emulate or avoid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and quality of required supplemental plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and content of supplemental plans such as data sharing plans, leadership plans, and other required plans (e.g., sharing plans, leadership plans, summary statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sample applications often include these plans—examine their scope, specificity, and alignment with NIH expectations. Note how they are integrated into the application and what level of detail reviewers found acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity with current NIH forms, policies, and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples may not reflect the latest NIH rules, policies, or formatting, so it's imperative you follow the latest official NIH How to Apply SF 424 instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not copy/paste samples without checking current requirements. For example, NIH's Data Management and Sharing (DMS) policy came into effect with FORMS-H and may be absent from earlier samples. NIH will transition to FORMS-I for applications due on or after Jan 25, 2025; account separately for policy and form changes (see High-Level Summary of Form Changes in FORMS-I). Follow the current SF424 and package-specific instructions for required components, page limits, and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sample applications as models of outstanding grantsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples are provided as examples of outstanding grantsmanship and demonstrate a successful approach to presenting a research plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat sample applications as illustrative models for tone, organization, and persuasive presentation, but adapt strategies to your project and current policy requirements rather than reproducing content verbatim.
